title: Review-slot race tests on windows-latest: trace and fix the cause of the slot_lock_timeout failures in both RaceTests (the slot lock stays held after a racer has finished) without skipping tests, weakening checks or adding retries for green (DB-150; D-090-R093/R094/R337/R338/R339)
objective: The windows-latest supervisor-bridge job (pytest tools/test_agent_supervisor_*.py) failed three times on 2026-10-06 in tools/test_agent_supervisor_review_slots.py::RaceTests: test_global_last_slot_never_double_taken twice (job 112160344138, run 37430612001, PR #448 head 486ebe8c; job 112164492630, run 37431907048 attempt 1, integration head 789f87ce) and test_per_lane_last_slot_never_double_taken once (job 112181006630, run 37436954274 attempt 1, integration head 4b6a4d8c, with no other CI run in progress). The racers now report reason codes (M0-T181), and in all three runs EVERY racer that was not admitted answered 'refused:slot_lock_timeout' after its own 30 s wait for the slot lock: 2 admitted + 4 timed out, twice; 1 admitted + 5 timed out, once. No run shows a last slot taken twice. The review-slots test file took about 62 s in each failing run. One manual rerun of each integration run passed (3952 passed). So the lock stayed unavailable for 30 s AFTER the admitted racers had already left the critical section and written their results. Under /deficit-convergence: work from the three frozen job logs, trace the complete causal path in the code (the runner is windows-latest; this host is Linux), decide with evidence whether the cause is test timing or a real defect in tools/agent_supervisor/review_slots.py (the lead to prove or rule out first: _SlotLock.release() leaves the lock file on disk, owned by a still-living process, when its single unlink - or the read before it - fails on Windows while another racer briefly has the file open, because the failure is swallowed), show the deciding platform behaviour on windows-latest itself, and fix the CAUSE as one bounded change. Reconcile the result with the two earlier records that looked at this code: M0-T176's report section 4 item 4 ('release's unlink - already correct, no change') and M0-T181's convergence record (Failure A classified as test-harness timing). Preserve every safety and concurrency assertion; never skip or weaken a test and never add a retry merely to obtain a green run (D-090-R094).
business_reason: Owner start prompt of 2026-10-06 (D-090 source-041): R339 'treat a tracked, reviewed fix of these tests as the first piece of work, because every merge now risks a red run'; R337 the stated fact that both race tests fail on CI, whose cause this task establishes; R338 'correct that record' (DB-150). Standing rules for this repair: D-090-R093 (bounded repair of the recurring Windows supervisor failures in a separate PR; test timing or a real supervisor defect; fix the cause) and D-090-R094 (preserve the safety and concurrency assertions; no skipped tests, weakened checks or retries for green). Supervisor freeze (.claude/rules/supervisor-freeze.md section 2) qualifying evidence: a failed acceptance scenario - the RACE scenario of M0-T171 failed on CI in jobs 112160344138, 112164492630 and 112181006630. Every merge to the integration branch runs this job; a red run blocks the fail-closed merge step.

ONE bounded change. If the cause is the release path: after a normal _SlotLock.release() the lock file is gone even when a concurrent short read briefly blocks the removal (a bounded wait derived from the lock's own timeout and poll values, never an unbounded loop); release still never removes or overwrites a lock whose lock_id is not its own; a release that cannot complete inside its bound stays fail-closed (nobody is admitted on a guess) and is observable rather than silent; an ADMITTED reservation that was already written is never turned into a refusal by a late lock-release problem (that would strand the slot); try_reserve / release / active return exactly what they returned before in every non-failing case. If the cause is elsewhere, the same standard applies to that site

new deterministic tests, runnable on any host: (i) the transient case - the removal fails N times with the Windows error and then succeeds -> the lock file is gone and the next acquire succeeds promptly; (ii) the never-clears case -> bounded, fail-closed, typed, no other holder's lock touched; (iii) a lock file carrying a different lock_id is left untouched; (iv) MUTATION PROOF: with the literal pre-repair release body restored, test (i) fails - the command and its output are in the producer report; (v) a real-handle test on Windows (skipped elsewhere with a stated reason) - that platform skip is the only skip added
